title: Cardio or Weight Training: Which Is Better for Fat Loss?
intro: Short answer: both are good, and combining both works best for most people. But fat comes off mainly when the energy coming in from food is slightly less than what you burn, so nutrition is still the main factor.
muscles: Cardio (brisk walking, stairs, skipping) trains your heart, lungs and stamina. Strength training (squat, push-up, bridge, plank) builds and maintains muscle throughout the body.
steps: Do bodyweight strength training 2-3 days a week: squats, push-ups, glute bridges, lunges and planks.
Do cardio 2-3 days a week, 20-30 minutes: brisk walking, climbing stairs or skipping.
Aim for daily steps, for example 6,000-8,000 steps depending on your ability.
Watch your plate: a quarter protein, a quarter rice, half vegetables, even when eating at a mamak or warung.
Take at least 1 rest day a week.
mistakes: Doing hours of cardio, then feeling super hungry and eating more than usual.
Lifting weights diligently but never looking at your food portions.
Changing programmes every week. Being consistent for 8-12 weeks matters more than a perfect programme.
easier: Start with 2 days of short strength training (15-20 minutes) and 15-20 minutes of walking on other days.
harder: Add a third strength training day, increase reps or sets, and switch some of your cardio to an interval version (HIIT).
dose: For beginners: 2-3 strength sessions of 20-30 minutes and 2-3 cardio sessions of 20-30 minutes a week, aiming for about 150 minutes of moderate activity a week.
safety: Stop if you have sharp joint pain, chest pain or dizziness. If you have a chronic condition like high blood pressure, diabetes or heart problems, talk to your doctor before starting.

faq.a: During the session, cardio usually burns more. But strength training helps keep your muscle while losing weight, so your body looks firmer. That's why combining both is best.

faq.q: Do I need to go to the gym to lift weights?
faq.a: No need. For beginners, your own bodyweight is challenging enough. Once you're stronger, you can use a backpack filled with water bottles or books.

faq.q: Why did my weight go up a bit when I started strength training?
faq.a: This is common. Muscles store more water and energy after a new workout. Look at the 3-4 week trend, measure your waist and notice how your clothes fit, not the number on one or two days.
